correctness.rationale: Each deleted curve is C* except C and D, each C* minus one point with Euler characteristic -1. In ABCD the only pairwise torus intersections are A∩B at (-1,-1) and C∩D at two primitive cube-root points; no triples, so χ(deleted)=-5 and χ(complement)=5. In ABCE only A∩B, A∩E, B∩E contribute three isolated points, giving χ=-4 and χ(complement)=4. Independent symbolic polynomial solving reproduced each pairwise intersection; independently reconstructed the saturated Groebner elimination over Q for exponent vector (2,3,5,7,11,13), giving squarefree degree-5 and degree-4 x eliminants with leading terms z,y,x^5 or z,y,x^4, excluding base divisor points. Huh signed Euler/ML-degree theorem applies since the loci are smooth very affine surfaces of complex dimension two and Cox monomial exponents induce generic logarithmic forms. Counting generic complex critical points does not assert all exponent vectors or real positive critical points. Different Euler characteristics obstruct isomorphism of these very affine loci only.
residual_risks: General ML-degree theorem is assumed as published mathematics; exceptions in nongeneric exponents not classified.

final_claim: For the two specific hexagonal toric positive-chart very affine loci T\V(ABCD) and T\V(ABCE) with T=(C*)^2, A=1+x, B=1+y, C=1+x+xy, D=1+y+xy, E=1+xy, their Euler characteristics (and generic logarithmic scattering/ML degrees) are exactly 5 and 4 respectively, making the very affine loci nonisomorphic, without claiming full affine charts nonisomorphic.
limitations: Specified pair of charts only; not all positive charts with a given hexagonal fan.
